headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from ms-swift feeding Prefect workflows; shared write/network surfaces create moderate conflict and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files, run shell/Python, and handle logs/configuration; Prefect orchestrates workflows and can consume upstream outputs. No shared channel is explicitly documented, but a file-based handoff is plausible and the rubric says uncertainty escalates. Prefect’s workflow role makes instruction-like content in ms-swift outputs a realistic injection path.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests ms-swift-generated files or logs as workflow inputs
IF ms-swift outputs are copied into Prefect task parameters without sanitization
mitigations: Separate handoff directories for generated artifacts and instructions
Strip or escape instruction-like text before Prefect ingestion
Require a schema validator on ms-swift outputs
Add a human review step for any workflow-control fields
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags across the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift explicitly touches secrets-like hub_token/sdk-token and broad file classes, while Prefect has broad network egress and API access. Even though no shared workspace is stated, a workflow bridge could move sensitive files or logs from ms-swift into Prefect, which can then transmit them. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ms-swift writes secrets-bearing logs or configs into a Prefect-visible path
IF Prefect tasks upload those artifacts to external APIs
mitigations: Redact secrets from ms-swift logs before persistence
Restrict Prefect tasks to non-sensitive artifact paths
Disable artifact upload for sensitive runs
Rotate any exposed hub_token or sdk-token immediately
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on workflow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has filesystem write and subprocess execution; Prefect has broad network egress and workflow orchestration. They do not both advertise unrestricted filesystem write to the same directory, and Prefect’s write scope is not stated, so high is not justified. Still, overlapping mutable workflow artifacts can conflict in default automation setups, especially without locking.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or artifact directory
IF Prefect retries tasks while ms-swift is mutating the same files
mitigations: Use per-agent working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make Prefect consume immutable snapshots only
Disable concurrent retries on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestrator, so it may treat ms-swift outputs as authoritative task inputs or metadata. ms-swift can generate evaluation outputs, logs, and configuration data, which Prefect could then route into downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so a bad ms-swift output can cascade through Prefect workflows, but the blast radius is workflow-level rather than clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF Prefect uses ms-swift outputs as task parameters or control metadata
IF downstream Prefect tasks act on those values without validation
mitigations: Validate ms-swift outputs against a strict schema
Require approval before downstream side effects
Add checksum or signature checks on handoff files
Log and alert on malformed control fields
requires-engineering: insert a verification task between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only docs-only verified, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. ms-swift handles hub_token/sdk-token and Prefect handles workflow metadata, but there is no evidence that regulated data classes flow between them. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming the pair context because no compliance mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into ms-swift and then persisted by Prefect
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention for workflow metadata
Review logs for accidental secret capture
Set explicit deletion windows for artifacts
requires-engineering: map data flows to compliance controls
